_about: The SEO policy `dh seo` enforces: every rule it checks (why, fix, whether a script can fix it, which owner facts it needs), every owner fact and owner-only action that goes to PENDING.md, and the crawler lists. Ranking #1 cannot be promised by anyone; what can be guaranteed is that nothing that is in our control is missing. Checked against Google Search Central, Bing and the 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey (Sept 2026): FAQ rich results were removed from Google on 2026-05-07 (FAQPage markup stays valid and still helps AI answers); HowTo, sitelinks search box and seven more types retired earlier; Google ignores llms.txt (harmless, some AI tools read it); ChatGPT search and Copilot retrieve from Bing's index; OpenAI's crawlers do not run JavaScript; Core Web Vitals good = LCP < 2.5 s, INP < 200 ms, CLS < 0.1 at p75.

ai_crawlers._note: retrieval bots fetch pages when someone asks an AI a question: blocking them removes the business from AI answers. Training bots only feed model training: the owner chooses (brief seo.ai_crawlers = allow | search-only); default allow = maximum visibility.

rules.title: The site tells every search engine to stay out
rules.why: robots.txt `Disallow: /` for all agents (or Googlebot) removes the whole site from Google and Bing.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` writes a robots file that allows crawling and lists the sitemap.

rules.title: A public page is marked noindex
rules.why: noindex (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag) keeps the page out of search results even when everything else is perfect.
rules.fix: Remove the noindex from the page's metadata. Previews stay noindex through DH_NOINDEX=1, never through code.

rules.title: No robots.txt
rules.why: Crawlers look for /robots.txt first; without it they get no sitemap pointer and no crawl rules.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` (app/robots.ts, or public/robots.txt for static sites).

rules.title: No sitemap, or robots.txt does not point to it
rules.why: The sitemap is how Google, Bing (and through Bing, ChatGPT and Copilot) discover every page quickly.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` (app/sitemap.ts from the plan) — then submit it in Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

rules.title: The sitemap does not match the site
rules.why: A sitemap that misses public pages, lists signed-in pages, or uses another host wastes crawl budget and confuses canonicals.
rules.fix: Generate it from the plan (`dh seo apply`) so it always equals the public routes on the production domain.

rules.title: Unknown URLs answer 200 (soft 404)
rules.why: Pages that do not exist must answer 404, or Google indexes empty duplicates and trusts the site less.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` adds app/not-found.tsx; never redirect every unknown URL to the home page.

rules.title: A preview or staging address can be indexed
rules.why: A preview (sslip.io, http, staging) indexed beside the real domain splits signals and can outrank it with duplicate content.
rules.fix: Set DH_NOINDEX=1 on the preview app (`dh deploy raw envset <app-uuid> DH_NOINDEX=1`, redeploy); the real domain never has it.

rules.title: More than one address serves the site
rules.why: http vs https or www vs no-www serving the same pages = duplicate content and split links.
rules.fix: One canonical host: redirect http→https and the other host → the canonical one (Coolify: Domains + redirect).

rules.title: The content only appears after JavaScript runs
rules.why: AI answer engines (OpenAI's crawlers, most others) do not run JavaScript; Google does, but later and less often. An empty server HTML is invisible to them.
rules.fix: Server-render or pre-render the pages (Next.js does by default; a Vite SPA needs prerendering or SSR).

rules.title: A page has no real title
rules.why: The <title> is the blue link in results and the strongest on-page signal; a missing or template title ("Create Next App") loses both.
rules.fix: Write a title per page in .deckhand/copy.json → seo.pages, then `dh seo apply`.

rules.title: Titles are too long, too short or duplicated
rules.why: Google shows about 60 characters; duplicates make pages compete with each other.
rules.fix: One unique title per page, 30–60 characters, the main service (and city for a local business) first, the brand last (the template adds it).

rules.title: Meta descriptions missing, duplicated or the wrong length
rules.why: The description is the ad copy under the link: it decides the click. Missing = Google picks random text.
rules.fix: One unique 70–160 character description per page (what, for whom, where, a reason to click) in copy.json → seo.pages.

rules.title: Canonical URL missing, relative or pointing elsewhere
rules.why: The canonical tells Google which URL gets the credit; a wrong one hands a page's ranking to another page.
rules.fix: Each page declares its own absolute canonical on the production domain (`dh seo apply` adds alternates.canonical per page).

rules.title: Canonicals point to a placeholder host
rules.why: Canonical URLs on localhost or an unset domain tell Google the real pages live elsewhere: nothing on the production domain ranks.
rules.fix: `dh brief set domain=…` then `dh seo apply` again (or set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL on the production app) and redeploy.

rules.title: The root layout sets a canonical every page inherits
rules.why: Next.js metadata is inherited: a canonical in app/layout makes EVERY page say it is the home page, so only the home page ranks.
rules.fix: Remove alternates.canonical from the root layout; set it per page.

rules.title: metadataBase is not set
rules.why: Without it Next.js cannot build absolute URLs for canonical, Open Graph and hreflang tags.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` sets metadataBase from the production URL (NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL).

rules.title: <html lang> missing or wrong
rules.why: The language attribute tells Google (and screen readers) which audience the page serves.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` sets it to the brief's first language.

rules.title: No mobile viewport
rules.why: Google indexes the mobile version; without a viewport the page renders as a zoomed-out desktop page.
rules.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> (Next.js adds it by default).

rules.title: meta keywords present
rules.why: Google has ignored meta keywords for over a decade; it only shows competitors your strategy.
rules.fix: Delete it; put the words in titles, headings and text instead.

rules.title: A client-component page cannot export metadata
rules.why: A page.tsx starting with 'use client' cannot have its own title, description or canonical.
rules.fix: Move the interactive part into a child component and keep page.tsx a server component with `export const metadata`.

rules.title: A dynamic page has no generateMetadata
rules.why: Every product/article/location page would share one title and description.
rules.fix: Add `export async function generateMetadata({ params })` returning a title, description and canonical per item.

rules.title: A page has no H1, or more than one
rules.why: One H1 that says what the page is about is the clearest topic signal after the title.
rules.fix: Exactly one H1 per page (compose and try-on keep the first heading as H1).

rules.title: Heading levels skip (h2 → h4)
rules.why: A clean outline helps crawlers and screen readers understand sections.
rules.fix: Keep headings in order.

rules.title: Images without useful alt text
rules.why: Alt text is how Google Images and AI understand photos; it is also required for accessibility.
rules.fix: Describe each meaningful image in a few words (≤125 characters, no keyword stuffing); decorative images get alt="".

rules.title: The home page says too little
rules.why: Thin pages rarely rank; AI answers quote pages that state facts plainly.
rules.fix: At least ~150 words on the home page that say what you do, for whom, where, and why you (first-hand, specific).

rules.title: The home page does not say what customers search for
rules.why: If the main service (and the city, for a local business) is not in the home title, H1 and text, Google cannot match the page to those searches.
rules.fix: Put the top keyword (brief seo.keywords[0]) and the city in the home title, H1 and first paragraph — naturally, once.

rules.title: Links say "click here" / "learn more"
rules.why: Link text tells Google what the target page is about.
rules.fix: Use descriptive link text ("see our wedding cakes").

rules.title: Important pages are not linked from the home page
rules.why: Pages with no internal links are found late and rank poorly.
rules.fix: Link every key page from the navigation or the home page (the plan's nav does this).

rules.title: No Organization / LocalBusiness structured data
rules.why: JSON-LD states who you are (name, logo, address, phone, hours, profiles) in a form Google, Bing and AI engines read without guessing.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` writes it from the brief's confirmed facts (never invented).

rules.title: Structured data is invalid or incomplete
rules.why: Invalid JSON-LD is ignored; missing required properties make it ineligible.
rules.fix: Regenerate with `dh seo apply`, or fix the reported property; confirm in Google's Rich Results Test after launch.

rules.title: No WebSite structured data (site name)
rules.why: Google uses WebSite name/alternateName to show your brand name above the result instead of the domain.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` adds it.

rules.title: No logo in the structured data
rules.why: Google shows the logo in knowledge panels and results; it needs a square image of at least 112×112 px on your site.
rules.fix: Provide the real logo (brief brand.logo), then `dh seo apply`.

rules.title: No sameAs profiles
rules.why: sameAs links (Instagram, Facebook, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn…) tie your website to your profiles as one entity — a strong trust and AI-answer signal.
rules.fix: Provide the profile URLs (brief brand.social / seo.profiles), then `dh seo apply`.

rules.title: Self-serving review markup
rules.why: Ratings/reviews marked up on your own Organization/LocalBusiness are not eligible for stars and can earn a manual action; invented ratings are fraud.
rules.fix: Remove aggregateRating/review from your own business markup; collect real reviews on your Google Business Profile.

rules.title: FAQ/HowTo markup added for rich results
rules.why: Google removed FAQ rich results on 2026-05-07 and HowTo earlier: no snippet will show. The markup still helps AI engines read real Q&A.
rules.fix: Keep FAQPage only for real questions shown on the page; expect no special result in Google.

rules.title: Products without Product markup
rules.why: Product markup with price, currency and availability makes products eligible for merchant listings and price-rich results.
rules.fix: Add Product JSON-LD per product page (name, image, description, offers.price, priceCurrency, availability) from real data.

rules.title: Name, address and phone are not on the site
rules.why: NAP on the site (footer + contact page) is what Google matches against your Business Profile and directories.
rules.fix: Show the exact same name, address and phone in the footer and on the contact page (facts from the brief).

rules.title: The site's name/address/phone differ from the brief
rules.why: Inconsistent NAP across the web makes Google (and AI local answers) unsure you are one business.
rules.fix: Use one spelling everywhere — the website, Google Business Profile, directories, social bios.

rules.title: Opening hours are not published
rules.why: Hours in text and in structured data answer "open now" searches and AI questions.
rules.fix: Give the hours (brief seo.local.hours); they go into the page and the LocalBusiness markup.

rules.title: No Open Graph image/title/description
rules.why: Shares on WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, iMessage show a blank card — fewer clicks, fewer links.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` adds app/opengraph-image (1200×630, your brand) and the Open Graph tags.

rules.title: No Twitter/X card
rules.why: Links shared on X show without a preview.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` adds twitter card = summary_large_image.

rules.title: Social profiles are not linked from the site
rules.why: Visitors and crawlers should find your profiles from the site, and the profiles should link back.
rules.fix: Provide the profile URLs; the footer shows them (sitelinks) and sameAs lists them.

rules.title: Languages are not linked with hreflang
rules.why: Without reciprocal hreflang (+ x-default) Google shows the wrong language or treats translations as duplicates.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` adds alternates.languages for every page and every language in the brief.

rules.title: Heavy images
rules.why: Large images are the first cause of a slow LCP (Core Web Vitals: good under 2.5 s).
rules.fix: Serve images through next/image (or AVIF/WebP), under ~300 KB, with width and height set.

rules.title: Images without width/height
rules.why: Missing dimensions make the page jump while loading (CLS, good under 0.1).
rules.fix: Use next/image or set width and height on every .

rules.title: No About or Contact page
rules.why: Who is behind the site and how to reach them are basic trust (E-E-A-T) signals for people, Google and AI answers.
rules.fix: Add both pages to the plan (real people, real contact details).

rules.title: No privacy policy / legal notice
rules.why: Required in many countries (GDPR, imprint laws) and a trust signal.
rules.fix: Add a privacy page (and an imprint where the law asks for one) to the plan.

rules.title: The production site is not on HTTPS
rules.why: HTTPS is a ranking signal and browsers mark http pages "Not secure".
rules.fix: A domain + Let's Encrypt (references/ops/20-domain-dns-ssl.md).

rules.title: AI answer engines are blocked
rules.why: Blocking OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot or Bingbot removes the business from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Copilot answers.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` allows the retrieval bots (training bots follow the owner's choice).

rules.title: No llms.txt
rules.why: Google ignores it (no harm, no gain); some AI tools read it as a clean summary of the site.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` writes public/llms.txt from the plan.

rules.title: No IndexNow key
rules.why: IndexNow tells Bing (the index behind ChatGPT search and Copilot), Yandex, Seznam and Naver about a change within minutes instead of days.
rules.fix: `dh seo apply` creates the key file; `dh deploy ship` pings IndexNow on every production release.

rules.title: The business facts are not stated plainly
rules.why: AI answers quote pages that say, in plain words, what you do, where, for whom and at what price.
rules.fix: One answer-first sentence near the top of the home page: "<Brand> is a <service> in <city> for <audience> — <proof>."

rules.title: nosnippet / max-snippet:0 present
rules.why: Snippet restrictions are the one control that removes a page from Google's AI Overviews and shortens its result.
rules.fix: Remove them unless the owner explicitly wants the page out of AI answers.

facts.label: The website address (domain)
facts.why: Canonical URLs, the sitemap, Open Graph and structured data all need the final address; a preview address must never be indexed.
facts.how: Buy or choose the domain (references/ops/20-domain-dns-ssl.md) and tell the agent — `dh brief set domain=example.com`.

facts.label: What customers type into Google to find you (3–5 phrases)
facts.why: Titles, H1s and the first paragraph are written for these phrases; guessing wrong wastes every page.
facts.how: The agent proposes them from the research (competitors' pages that rank); you confirm or correct: `dh brief set seo.keywords="wedding cakes lyon,custom cakes lyon,…"`.

facts.label: The cities or areas you serve
facts.why: Local searches are "service + city"; the city must be in titles, text and structured data (areaServed).

facts.label: Your primary business category (the same one as on Google Business Profile)
facts.why: The primary category is the #1 factor for Google's local pack (2026 Local Search Ranking Factors); the website's LocalBusiness type should match it.
facts.how: Pick the most specific category Google offers (e.g. "Bakery", not "Store"): `dh brief set seo.local.category=Bakery`.

facts.label: Business address (or "service area only" if customers never visit)
facts.why: Name, address and phone must be identical on the site, Google Business Profile and directories.
facts.how: `dh brief set seo.local.address="12 Rue X, 69001 Lyon, FR"` — or `seo.local.address=service-area`.

facts.label: Public phone number
facts.why: Part of NAP; click-to-call on mobile; LocalBusiness telephone.

facts.label: Opening hours
facts.why: Answers "open now" and "hours" searches and AI questions; LocalBusiness openingHours.

facts.label: Public contact email
facts.why: Contact page and structured data; a trust signal.
facts.how: `dh brief set seo.local.email=hello@example.com` (on your own domain if possible).

facts.label: Price range (e.g. €€ or "from €25")
facts.why: Shown in local results and read by AI answers.

facts.label: Your real logo (square, at least 112×112 px)
facts.why: Used by Google for the logo in results and knowledge panels, and for the favicon.
facts.how: Put the file in public/ and `dh brief set brand.logo=/logo.png`.

facts.label: Your social profile links (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube…)
facts.why: Profiles linked both ways + sameAs make the business one entity to Google and AI engines; also the footer links.
facts.how: `dh brief set brand.social="https://instagram.com/x,https://facebook.com/x"` — only profiles you actually use.

facts.label: Your listings (Google Business Profile, Yelp/Tripadvisor/industry directories, Apple Maps, Bing Places)
facts.why: Citations with the same NAP confirm you exist and where; the GBP link goes into sameAs.

facts.label: Who is behind the business (name, one-line bio, photo)
facts.why: Real people with real experience (E-E-A-T) are what Google's quality systems and AI answers trust.
facts.how: `dh brief set seo.founder="Marie Dupont — pastry chef since 2009"` + a photo in public/.

facts.label: Real photos (storefront, team, products, work)
facts.why: First-hand images rank in Google Images, feed Business Profile and prove you are real; stock photos do none of that.
facts.how: Drop them in public/photos/ and tell the agent what each shows (it writes the alt text).

facts.label: Where your real reviews live (and permission to quote a few)
facts.why: Reviews are the #2 local ranking factor; quoted testimonials convert — but only real ones, never marked up as your own rating.
facts.how: `dh brief set seo.reviews="Google Business Profile"`; say which reviews may be quoted with first name.

actions.label: Verify the site in Google Search Console and submit the sitemap
actions.why: The only way to see what Google indexes, which searches show you, and to fix errors fast.
actions.how: search.google.com/search-console → Add property → Domain → copy the TXT record and give it to the agent (it adds the DNS record through the provider API) → Verify → Sitemaps → submit https://<domain>/sitemap.xml. Then `dh brief set seo.search_console=verified`.

actions.label: Add the site to Bing Webmaster Tools
actions.why: Bing's index is a main source for ChatGPT search and the source for Microsoft Copilot: not in Bing = missing from those AI answers.
actions.how: bing.com/webmasters → Sign in → Import from Google Search Console (one click) → confirm the sitemap. Then `dh brief set seo.bing=verified`.

actions.label: Claim and complete your Google Business Profile
actions.why: Business Profile signals are about a third of local pack ranking; a 100% complete profile gets far more clicks.
actions.how: business.google.com → Add your business → the SAME name, address, phone and primary category as the website → verify (video or postcard) → hours, services, photos, website URL → share the review link with customers. Then `dh brief set seo.gbp=claimed`.

actions.label: List the business on Bing Places and Apple Business Connect
actions.why: Bing Places feeds Bing/Copilot/ChatGPT local answers; Apple Business Connect feeds Apple Maps and Siri.
actions.how: bingplaces.com → Import from Google Business Profile · businessconnect.apple.com → Add location. Then `dh brief set seo.places=done`.

actions.label: Ask your first real customers for Google reviews
actions.why: Review count, recency and replies are the second strongest local factor; never buy, filter or incentivise reviews.
actions.how: Business Profile → Ask for reviews → share the link with your last 10 happy customers; reply to every review. The `review-request` bot (`dh ops add review-request`) can send the link after each order or booking. Then `dh brief set seo.reviews_asked=yes`.
